$comment: Package boundaries of the workspace, the single source for the dependency-cruiser rules, the ESLint architecture rules and the architecture tests. Paths ending in / are folders, all other paths are files. tests/architecture/boundaries.mts checks this file before anything uses it.

egress.description: The single outbound path of core: the only code that opens network connections, after it checks the host allow-list.

transportBuilders.description: The composition root: the only code outside the outbound path that imports the factory of the HTTP transport, the subpath ./http of core, and the only code at all that imports the stderr writer, the logger and the audit sink through the subpath ./composition of core. Each entry is a folder of the command line.

httpDouble.description: The test double for ChurchTools in testkit: the only code outside the outbound path that imports the transport on a MockAgent, the subpath ./http/testing of core. One folder directly under src/ of testkit.

rawClientImporters.description: Core modules outside the client folder that may import the raw client. Each entry is one file, added when the module exists.

mcpMount.description: The mount: the only registration with the MCP SDK, next to the serialize stage. Reached through the subpath export ./mcp of core.

mcpRegistration.description: The only modules that call the registration functions of the MCP SDK. Each entry is one file inside the mount or inside the package for tests, there the server of the elicitation spike (ADR 0053).

mcpMountImporters.description: Code outside the mount folder that may import the mount.

mcpSdk.description: Code that may import the MCP SDK: the mount, the server and, in the package for tests, the elicitation spike (ADR 0053).

stdioEntries.description: Start of the stdio mode, in which stdout carries only the MCP protocol, and the start of the elicitation spike. Nothing reachable from here may be a stdout place.

stdioReachable.description: Modules of the command line that the start over stdio may import: the start notices and the catalog of their texts. Nothing reachable from here may be a stdout place, already before the start imports them.

stdout.description: Code that may write to stdout.

stderr.description: Code that may write to stderr: the logger, the messages of the command line for operators, the start notices of the command line, which the start over stdio may reach, and the start of the elicitation spike, which writes its record there.

plugins.description: Plugins as a third party would write them: the example plugin in testkit, and the plugin of the free core with its tools in the tools package. Of the packages of the workspace they may import only the plugin API. This rule leaves npm packages such as zod, which every plugin brings itself, to the other rules.

moduleState.description: Modules that may keep mutable state at module level. Each entry is one file with its own ADR.

utilModule.description: Files that may load node:util, whose ES module makes fd 2 non-blocking: the command of the command line for parseArgs and the canary values of testkit, which use inspect. Each entry is one file in the command line or in testkit, outside the places of the start over stdio.

environment.description: Code that may read the environment and the arguments of the process: only the entry of the command line, which hands them to the core as parameters. Other code could otherwise read the token from them past the Secret.
